name: Back Extension
instructions: Set yourself in a back-extension bench with the pads just below the hip bones.
Cross the arms over the chest and let the torso hang, keeping the spine long.
Squeeze the glutes and raise the torso until the body forms one straight line.
Stop at that line — lifting past it arches the low back and is where this goes wrong.
Lower under control until you feel the hamstrings and low back lengthen.
coaching_cue: Stop at a straight line. Arching past it is where this goes wrong.

progression.harder: Back Extension holding a plate to the chest

clinical_rationale: Repeated lumbar extension. Prone position rules it out prenatally.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Band Lat Pulldown
instructions: Anchor a band overhead — a door anchor or a sturdy bar both work.
Kneel or sit below it and hold an end in each hand with the arms overhead.
Pull the hands down and out toward the shoulders, driving the elbows toward the ribs.
Control the band back overhead until the arms are straight again.
coaching_cue: The closest a home setup gets to a pulldown. Keep the torso still.

progression.easier: a lighter band, or kneel further from the anchor

clinical_rationale: Overhead, but band tension is lowest at the top where the shoulder is most vulnerable.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band, or kneel further from the anchor. Too easy? Move to Pull-Up.

name: Barbell Shrug
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell at arm's length in front of the thighs, hands shoulder-width apart.
Set the shoulders back and keep the arms completely straight throughout.
Lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears as far as they will travel.
Pause for a full second at the top — the traps respond to the hold, not the bounce.
Lower slowly until the shoulders are fully relaxed down.
coaching_cue: Pause at the top for a second — traps respond to the hold, not the bounce.
clinical_rationale: Heavy load hanging from the shoulder girdle, transmitted through the neck.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand with the feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips to about 45 degrees with the spine long and the knees slightly bent.
Let both dumbbells hang beneath the shoulders with the palms facing in.
Row them to the ribs by driving the elbows back and past the torso.
Lower under control to straight arms, holding the back angle steady the whole time.
coaching_cue: Hinge to about 45 degrees and hold it — the back angle should not change as you row.
clinical_rationale: Unsupported hinge under load.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Doorway Row
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy door frame and take hold of it at chest height with one hand.
Place the feet either side of the frame, close to it, and lean back with the arm straight.
Pull yourself upright by driving the elbow back, keeping the body in one line.
Lower back to a straight arm under control, then change sides.
coaching_cue: No bar, no band, still a real row. Walk the feet forward to make it harder.

progression.easier: stand more upright, feet closer to the frame

clinical_rationale: Self-limiting and light — the resistance is your own lean.
modification: Too hard? Use stand more upright, feet closer to the frame. Too easy? Move to Inverted Row.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell hanging at each side, palms facing the thighs.
Set the shoulders back and keep the arms straight and relaxed.
Raise both shoulders straight up toward the ears as high as they will go.
Hold for a second at the top, then lower slowly.
Move straight up and down — rolling the shoulders adds nothing but wear.
coaching_cue: Straight up and down. Rolling the shoulders adds nothing but wear.
clinical_rationale: As the barbell shrug.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Prone Swimmer
instructions: Lie face down with the arms extended overhead and the forehead resting on the mat.
Lift both arms a few centimetres off the floor and keep them there.
Sweep one arm out to the side and down toward the hip, then back overhead.
Move slowly and keep the hips and ribs pressed into the floor.
Alternate arms for the prescribed time — this is upper-back endurance, not a lift.
coaching_cue: Small movement, slow tempo. This is upper-back endurance work, not a lift.
clinical_rationale: Light, but performed face down.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Rack Pull
instructions: Set the safety pins in a rack at about knee height and rest a loaded barbell on them.
Stand with the feet hip-width apart, shins against the bar, and take an overhand grip outside the knees.
Set the chest up and the spine long, then drive through the floor to stand tall.
Finish with the hips and knees locked and the shoulders back, without leaning backwards.
Lower the bar to the pins under control rather than dropping it.
coaching_cue: Bar starts at knee height. It is a deadlift with the hardest part removed.
clinical_rationale: Heaviest axial load in the library. Breath-holding against a maximal pull is the mechanism.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Renegade Row
instructions: Start in a push-up position with a hand on each dumbbell, feet wider than the hips for balance.
Brace the trunk hard so the hips stay level and square to the floor.
Row one dumbbell to the ribs while pressing the other firmly into the ground.
Refuse to let the hips rotate — if they do, widen the feet or go lighter.
Lower the dumbbell under control and repeat on the other side.
coaching_cue: Widen the feet for stability and refuse to let the hips rotate.
clinical_rationale: A plank under a rowing load; the trunk and the supporting shoulder both work hard.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
instructions: Stand facing a high pulley with a straight bar attached, feet hip-width apart.
Take an overhand grip and step back about half a metre until the arms are extended overhead.
Hinge forward slightly from the hips, keeping the elbows just short of locked.
Keeping the arms long, pull the bar down in an arc until it reaches the thighs.
Return along the same arc under control — the moment the elbows bend, it becomes a pushdown.
coaching_cue: Arms stay long. The moment the elbows bend it becomes a pushdown.
clinical_rationale: Long-lever shoulder extension; the straight arm is what makes it a shoulder movement.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Superman Hold
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with the arms extended overhead and the legs straight.
Draw the shoulders down away from the ears and lengthen through the spine.
Lift the arms, chest and legs a few centimetres off the floor at the same time.
Think long rather than high — reach away through the fingers and toes.
Hold, breathing normally, then lower everything together under control.
coaching_cue: Lift by lengthening, not by cranking the low back — think long, not high.

progression.easier: lift only the arms, keeping the legs down
progression.harder: Superman Hold with a longer hold

clinical_rationale: Sustained lumbar extension, performed lying face down.
modification: Too hard? Use lift only the arms, keeping the legs down. Too easy? Move to Superman Hold with a longer hold.

name: V-Bar Pulldown
instructions: Sit at a pulldown machine with the thighs secured under the pads.
Take a close neutral grip on the V-handle with the arms extended overhead.
Lean the torso back no more than about 15 degrees and keep it there.
Pull the handle to the upper chest by driving the elbows down toward the ribs.
Return slowly to full arm extension, letting the shoulder blades rise at the top.
coaching_cue: The close neutral grip is kinder to the shoulder than a wide bar.
clinical_rationale: Neutral close grip is the kindest overhead pull; keeps `shoulder_injury` but not the cuff tag.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Wall Angel Row
instructions: Stand with the back flat against a wall and the feet a few centimetres out from it.
Press the low back, upper back and head into the wall and keep all three in contact.
Set the arms against the wall with the elbows bent to 90 degrees at shoulder height.
Draw the elbows down and back into the wall, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Return to the start slowly — if the low back lifts away, you have gone too far.
coaching_cue: Keep the low back flat against the wall; if it arches, you have gone too far.
clinical_rationale: Postural drill against a wall. Suitable for almost everyone, including prenatally.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Band Row
instructions: Anchor a band at chest height, or sit on the floor and loop it around your feet.
Hold an end in each hand with the arms extended and the shoulders back.
Pull both hands to the ribs by driving the elbows straight back.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for a beat, then extend the arms under control.
coaching_cue: Elbows past the ribs, chest tall. Do not let the shoulders round forward at the end.
clinical_rationale: Upright, light, and fully self-limiting.
modification: Too hard? Use step closer to the anchor. Too easy? Move to Inverted Row.

name: Bent Over Barbell Row
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip just outside the knees.
Push the hips back and hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees, keeping the spine long and the knees soft.
Let the bar hang at arm's length, then pull it to the navel by driving the elbows back.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top without letting the torso rise to meet the bar.
Lower the bar under control until the arms are straight and the shoulder blades travel forward.
coaching_cue: Bar to the belly button. If the torso rises to meet it, the weight is winning.
clinical_rationale: Sustained loaded spinal flexion hold; the hinge position is also unavailable as the abdomen grows.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Chest Supported Dumbbell Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie chest-down on it with the feet braced.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with the arms hanging straight down, palms facing in.
Pull the shoulder blades together first, then row both dumbbells to the ribs.
Pause at the top with the elbows past the torso.
Lower slowly to straight arms — the bench holds your position, so the back does all the work.
coaching_cue: The bench holds your torso so the back does all the pulling.
clinical_rationale: The bench removes the spinal load entirely. This is the row that survives a back restriction.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Take an underhand grip on a bar, hands roughly shoulder-width apart.
Hang at full arm extension with the shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
Pull the elbows down to the ribs until the chin clears the bar.
Keep the ribs down and avoid swinging the legs to generate momentum.
Lower under control all the way to straight arms.
coaching_cue: Underhand grip brings the biceps in, which is why it is the easier of the two.
clinical_rationale: As the pull-up, with the supinated grip adding elbow load.
modification: Too hard? Use Inverted Row, then band-assisted chin-ups. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Set a bar at roughly hip height in a rack, or use the edge of a sturdy table.
Lie underneath it and take an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk the feet out until the body is straight and the arms are fully extended.
Pull the chest to the bar by driving the elbows down and back, keeping the hips level.
Pause when the chest touches, then lower under control to full arm extension.
coaching_cue: The more horizontal your body, the harder it is. Walk the feet in to make it easier.

progression.easier: Inverted Row with the bar set higher

clinical_rationale: Bodyweight, spine neutral and supported by the feet. Among the safest pulls in the library.
modification: Too hard? Use Inverted Row with the bar set higher. Too easy? Move to Inverted Row with feet elevated.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, with the other foot on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in the free hand with the arm hanging straight down.
Keep the torso square to the floor and the spine long.
Row the dumbbell to the hip, not the shoulder, driving the elbow past the ribs.
Lower under control to a full stretch, then complete the set before changing sides.
coaching_cue: Row to the hip, not the shoulder, and keep the torso square to the floor.
clinical_rationale: The bench takes most of the spinal load, so the disc restriction is dropped; still a hinged position.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Pull-Up
instructions: Take an overhand grip on a bar slightly wider than the shoulders.
Hang at full arm extension and pull the shoulders down away from the ears.
Drive the elbows down toward the ribs until the chest approaches the bar.
Keep the body still — a swing turns this into a different exercise.
Lower slowly to straight arms before the next repetition.
coaching_cue: Chest to the bar, shoulders away from the ears at the top.
clinical_rationale: Full overhead hang loads the shoulder at end range; hanging is also avoided as the abdomen loads.
modification: Too hard? Use Inverted Row, then band-assisted pull-ups. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit at the machine with the feet braced and take the handle with the arms extended.
Sit tall with a long spine and a slight forward lean at the start.
Pull the handle to the navel by driving the elbows back past the ribs.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together, then extend the arms slowly.
Let the shoulder blades travel forward at the end of each rep rather than holding them locked.
coaching_cue: Sit tall and let the shoulder blades travel — do not row with a locked upper back.
clinical_rationale: Seated and supported; the low back still works to hold the torso upright.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: T-Bar Row
instructions: Stand over the bar with the feet either side and take the handle with both hands.
Hinge forward from the hips to about 45 degrees, keeping the spine long and the knees soft.
Let the weight hang at arm's length beneath the chest.
Row the handle to the lower ribs by driving the elbows back.
Lower under control to straight arms, holding the back angle steady throughout.
coaching_cue: Chest supported where possible — it takes the low back out of the equation.
clinical_rationale: Same hinged position as a barbell row.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit at a pulldown machine and secure the thighs under the pads.
Take an overhand grip on the bar noticeably wider than the shoulders, arms extended overhead.
Set the chest up and lean back only slightly, keeping that angle for the whole set.
Pull the bar to the collarbone by driving the elbows down and out, not by leaning further back.
Return to full extension under control, allowing the shoulder blades to travel up.
coaching_cue: Pull the bar to the collarbone by driving the elbows down, not by leaning back.
clinical_rationale: Overhead start position. Seated and supported, so no prenatal restriction.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Band Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet hip-width apart.
Hold an end in each hand with the arms at your sides and the palms facing forward.
Curl both hands toward the shoulders, keeping the elbows pinned to your sides.
Lower slowly against the band's pull until the arms are straight.
coaching_cue: Bands get harder as you curl, which is exactly where the biceps is strongest.
clinical_rationale: Tension is lowest at full extension, where the elbow is most exposed.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band. Too easy? Move to Dumbbell Bicep Curl.

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar hang at arm's length with the elbows tucked against the ribs.
Curl the bar toward the chest, keeping the elbows pinned in place.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until the arms are straight.
If the elbows drift forward or the hips swing, the weight is too heavy.
coaching_cue: Elbows stay at your sides. If they drift forward, the shoulders are helping.
clinical_rationale: Fixed supinated grip gives the elbow and wrist no room to adjust.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand about a foot-length back from the machine.
Take an underhand grip and let the arms hang straight with the elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar toward the shoulders without letting the elbows travel forward.
Squeeze at the top, where cable tension is highest.
Lower under control against the pull until the arms are fully straight.
coaching_cue: Tension never drops, so the last two reps are honest.
clinical_rationale: Constant tension holds the elbow under load through the whole range.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand about a foot-length back from the machine.
Take an end of the rope in each hand with the palms facing one another and the elbows at your sides.
Curl the hands toward the shoulders, keeping the elbows pinned and the wrists neutral.
Squeeze at the top and pull the ends of the rope slightly apart.
Lower under control against the cable until the arms are straight.
coaching_cue: Neutral grip on the rope, and pull the ends apart at the top.
clinical_rationale: Neutral grip with constant tension; the kindest loaded curl.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Concentration Curls
instructions: Sit on the end of a bench with the feet wide and a dumbbell in one hand.
Brace the back of that upper arm against the inside of the same-side thigh.
Let the arm hang straight, then curl the dumbbell toward the shoulder.
Turn the palm up as you lift and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly to a straight arm, then finish the set before changing sides.
coaching_cue: Elbow braced on the thigh; no swinging available, which is the idea.
clinical_rationale: Braced arm removes the escape route the standing versions allow.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand hanging at arm's length, palms facing in.
Tuck the elbows against the ribs and keep them there throughout.
Curl the weights up, turning the palms to face the ceiling as you lift.
Squeeze at the top with the dumbbells at shoulder height.
Lower slowly, reversing the rotation, until the arms are straight.
coaching_cue: Supinate as you lift — turning the palm up is half the movement.
clinical_rationale: Free rotation lets the wrist and elbow find a comfortable path.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding an EZ-bar on the inner angled grips, palms facing up and forward.
Let the bar hang at arm's length with the elbows against the ribs.
Curl the bar toward the chest without letting the elbows move forward.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control to straight arms.
The angled grip sits the wrists in a more comfortable position than a straight bar.
coaching_cue: The angled bar is easier on the wrists than a straight one.
clinical_rationale: The angled bar eases the wrist; the elbow load is unchanged.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Hammer Curls
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Keep the elbows tucked at your sides and the wrists neutral throughout.
Curl both dumbbells toward the shoulders without rotating the palms.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to straight arms — the neutral grip works the forearm as much as the biceps.
coaching_cue: Neutral grip throughout; this one builds the forearm as much as the biceps.
clinical_rationale: Neutral grip is the most forgiving curl for the elbow and wrist.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Inverted Row - Underhand Grip
instructions: Set a bar at roughly hip height and lie underneath it.
Take an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart, palms facing you.
Walk the feet out until the body is straight and the arms are extended.
Pull the chest to the bar, leading with the elbows and keeping the hips level.
Lower under control until the arms are straight again.
coaching_cue: The underhand grip is what puts the biceps in charge of a bodyweight pull.
clinical_rationale: As the inverted row; the supinated grip loads the elbow.
modification: Too hard? Use set the bar higher. Too easy? Move to Chin-Up.

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Set the preacher bench so the top of the pad sits under the armpits when seated.
Rest the backs of both upper arms flat on the pad and take an underhand grip on the bar.
Curl the bar toward the shoulders, keeping the arms in contact with the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Stop just short of a locked elbow at the bottom — slamming into full extension is what the elbow objects to.
coaching_cue: Do not slam into full extension at the bottom — the elbow does not enjoy it.
clinical_rationale: Loads the elbow at full extension, where the joint is least protected.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Self-Resisted Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand tall and place one hand palm-up at waist height, elbow tucked against your side.
Press the other palm down on top of it to create resistance.
Curl the lower hand toward the shoulder while the upper hand pushes back against it.
Push down hard enough that the last two reps are a genuine fight.
Lower slowly under the same resistance, then change sides.
coaching_cue: Push down with the free hand hard enough that the last rep is a fight.
clinical_rationale: The practitioner sets the resistance, so it cannot exceed what they tolerate.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Standing Dumbbell Reverse Curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and the palms facing your thighs, knuckles forward.
Keep the elbows tucked and the wrists straight and firm.
Curl both dumbbells toward the shoulders with the palms staying down.
Pause at the top without letting the wrists collapse backwards.
Lower slowly to straight arms — go lighter than a normal curl, the forearm is the limit here.
coaching_cue: Overhand grip. Go lighter than a normal curl — the forearm is the limit.
clinical_rationale: Pronated grip loads the lateral elbow — the tennis-elbow mechanism.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Towel Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand on one end of a towel and hold the other end in one hand, palm up.
Keep the elbow pinned to your side and curl the hand toward the shoulder.
Push down through the foot to resist as you curl, making the movement hard.
Lower slowly under the same resistance, then change sides.
coaching_cue: You set the resistance with the foot — make the last two reps a genuine fight.
clinical_rationale: As above — self-limiting by construction.
modification: Too hard? Use Self-Resisted Biceps Curl. Too easy? Move to Band Biceps Curl.

name: Air Bike
instructions: Sit on the bike, set the seat so the knee is almost straight at the bottom of the stroke.
Take the handles and start turning the pedals easily for a minute to warm up.
Drive with the legs and pull and push with the arms together.
Work at the effort the interval calls for — the resistance rises with how hard you go.
Ease back to an easy spin between intervals rather than stopping dead.
coaching_cue: Brutal and completely self-limiting — you can only go as hard as you can.
clinical_rationale: Self-limiting and non-impact, but the effort ceiling is as high as anything here.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Battle Ropes
instructions: Take an end of the rope in each hand and stand facing the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit into a quarter squat with the chest up and the trunk braced.
Drive one arm down as the other comes up, sending alternating waves along the rope.
Keep the hips low and let the arms work independently.
Maintain the wave for the prescribed time rather than chasing height.
coaching_cue: Stay in a quarter squat and let the arms work independently.
clinical_rationale: Sustained shoulder work at a cardiovascular intensity.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Brisk Walking
instructions: Set off at a pace that feels purposeful rather than casual.
Stand tall with the shoulders relaxed and let the arms swing naturally.
Aim for an effort where talking takes a little work but is still possible.
Take the first and last two minutes easier to warm up and cool down.
Keep the pace steady rather than surging and slowing.
coaching_cue: Fast enough that talking takes effort; slow enough that you could still do it.
clinical_rationale: The most universally available conditioning there is. No restriction in the library excludes it.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Burpees
instructions: Stand tall, then squat down and place both hands on the floor in front of the feet.
Jump or step the feet back into a plank with the body in one straight line.
Jump or step the feet back in toward the hands.
Stand or jump up to finish the repetition.
Pace it from the first rep — burpees punish anyone who starts at a sprint.
coaching_cue: Pace it. Burpees punish anyone who starts at a sprint.
clinical_rationale: Maximal-effort whole-body work combining landing impact with a floor transition.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Elliptical Trainer
instructions: Step onto the pedals and hold the moving handles with a light grip, standing tall.
Start pedalling at an easy pace for two to three minutes to warm up.
Raise the resistance until the effort feels moderate but you could still speak in short sentences.
Keep the whole foot in contact with the pedal and drive with the legs rather than pulling with the arms.
Lower the resistance for the final two minutes to bring the breathing back down.
coaching_cue: Supported and low impact, which is why it survives most joint restrictions.
clinical_rationale: Supported, non-impact, and among the better prenatal options. **Flagged for review** — the merged duplicate said otherwise.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: HIIT Circuit
instructions: Choose four movements you can perform safely without close attention to form.
Work at a hard but controlled effort on the first for the prescribed interval.
Move to the next with a short rest between, keeping the transitions brisk.
Complete all four to finish one round, then rest fully before the next.
The rest is part of the prescription — cutting it short makes this easier, not harder.
coaching_cue: Rest is part of the prescription — cutting it short makes it easier, not harder.
clinical_rationale: Sustained high effort with form degrading as the circuit progresses.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: High Knees
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the arms bent at your sides.
Drive one knee up toward hip height while pushing off the opposite foot.
Land softly on the ball of the foot and immediately drive the other knee up.
Stay light and quick, keeping the chest up rather than leaning back.
Continue alternating at a steady rhythm for the prescribed time.
coaching_cue: Drive the knees to hip height and stay light on the feet.
clinical_rationale: Running mechanics in place; landing force through knee and ankle.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
instructions: Set the treadmill to a walking pace you could hold a conversation at.
Raise the incline until the effort feels moderate but sustainable.
Walk tall without holding the handrails, letting the arms swing naturally.
Lower the incline for the last two minutes to bring the heart rate down.
coaching_cue: The incline does the work, not the speed. Hands off the rails.
clinical_rationale: Walking mechanics with the incline raising the effort rather than the impact.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Jump Rope
instructions: Hold a handle in each hand with the rope resting on the floor behind your heels.
Set the elbows close to the ribs and turn the rope with the wrists, not the whole arm.
Jump about an inch off the ground off the balls of the feet as the rope comes round.
Land softly with the knees slightly bent and keep the turning pace steady.
Start with short bouts of twenty to thirty seconds and build up as the coordination comes.
coaching_cue: Small hops off the balls of the feet — an inch is plenty.
clinical_rationale: Repetitive landing impact at high frequency.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Jumping Jacks
instructions: Stand tall with the feet together and the arms at your sides.
Jump the feet out wider than the hips while sweeping the arms overhead.
Land softly through the whole foot with the knees slightly bent.
Jump the feet back together and bring the arms down.
Keep a steady rhythm and stay relaxed through the shoulders.
coaching_cue: Land softly through the whole foot, knees slightly bent.
clinical_rationale: Repeated bilateral landing with the arms overhead.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Mountain Climbers
instructions: Start in a push-up position with the hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Brace the trunk and draw one knee toward the chest without letting the hips rise.
Switch legs, driving the other knee forward as the first foot returns to the floor.
Keep alternating at a steady rhythm, breathing continuously, for the prescribed time.
Keep the shoulders stacked over the hands throughout rather than drifting behind them.
coaching_cue: Hips stay low and level; do not let them bounce up with each drive.
clinical_rationale: Plank position held under a cardiovascular load; shoulders support throughout.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Sit on the seat, strap the feet in, and take the handle with an overhand grip.
Start compressed at the front with the shins vertical and the arms straight.
Drive with the legs first, then swing the torso back, then pull the arms to the ribs.
Reverse that order coming forward: arms away, torso over, then let the knees bend.
Keep the spine long throughout rather than rounding at either end of the stroke.
coaching_cue: Legs, then back, then arms — and the reverse on the way in.
clinical_rationale: Repeated loaded hinge at high cadence, where form fails as fatigue arrives.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Sprint Intervals (HIIT)
instructions: Warm up with three to five minutes of easy jogging or cycling.
Accelerate to near-maximal effort and hold it for twenty to thirty seconds.
Ease right down to a walk or slow jog for the recovery period.
Repeat the cycle for the prescribed number of rounds.
Finish with three minutes easy — maximal effort by definition, so if you can talk, it is not this.
coaching_cue: Maximal effort by definition. If you can hold a conversation it is not this.
clinical_rationale: Near-maximal cardiovascular effort with running impact.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Stair Climbing
instructions: Step onto the machine and start at a slow pace to find your rhythm.
Stand tall with the shoulders back and let the hands rest lightly on the rails for balance only.
Take full steps, driving through the whole foot rather than the toes.
Raise the speed until the effort is moderate and you could still speak in short sentences.
Ease the pace back for the final two minutes to bring the heart rate down.
coaching_cue: Stand tall and stay off the handrails — leaning on them halves the work.
clinical_rationale: Repeated single-leg knee extension under bodyweight.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Stationary Cycling
instructions: Set the saddle so that at the bottom of the pedal stroke the knee is almost straight, with a slight bend.
Sit tall with a light grip on the handlebars and the shoulders relaxed.
Pedal easily for two to three minutes to warm up before adding resistance.
Raise the resistance until the effort is moderate and sustainable, keeping a smooth cadence.
Ease the resistance off for the last few minutes to cool down.
coaching_cue: Low impact and easy to regulate — the default when joints are the limit.
clinical_rationale: Non-impact and fully supported; resistance is chosen.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Swimming
instructions: Warm up with two to three easy lengths at a conversational pace.
Swim at a steady effort you could sustain, breathing on a regular rhythm.
Rest for twenty to thirty seconds at the wall whenever you need to.
Finish with a slow length to bring the breathing back down.
coaching_cue: The most joint-friendly conditioning there is, which is why it survives almost every restriction.
clinical_rationale: Non-weight-bearing. Survives essentially every musculoskeletal restriction.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Barbell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor beneath a barbell in a rack set low, knees bent and feet flat.
Grip the bar a little wider than the shoulders and unrack it over the chest.
Lower until the backs of the upper arms rest on the floor.
Pause there for a beat rather than bouncing off the ground.
Press back to straight arms — the floor caps the range, which is what makes this shoulder-friendly.
coaching_cue: Pause when the triceps touch the floor rather than bouncing off it.
clinical_rationale: Supine, so not prenatal — but the floor caps the range, which is why it carries no shoulder restriction: it is the press a restricted shoulder keeps.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Cable Crossover
instructions: Set both pulleys above head height and take a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a split stance with the arms out wide and the elbows softly bent.
Bring the hands down and together in front of the hips in a wide arc.
Squeeze the chest with the hands together, keeping the elbow angle fixed.
Return along the same arc under control until you feel the chest lengthen.
coaching_cue: Finish with the hands together and the chest squeezed, not the arms locked.
clinical_rationale: Standing, so no supine restriction, but the same end-range shoulder position as a fly.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Chest Dip
instructions: Take hold of parallel bars and press up to straight arms with the feet crossed behind.
Lean the torso forward about 30 degrees and let the elbows travel out slightly.
Lower until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Stop there — going deeper puts the shoulder in its most vulnerable position.
Press back to straight arms, keeping the forward lean throughout.
coaching_cue: Lean the torso forward about 30 degrees; upright turns it into a triceps movement.
clinical_rationale: Deep shoulder extension under bodyweight — the position most associated with anterior shoulder strain.
modification: Too hard? Use Bench Dips. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Decline Push-Up
instructions: Set the feet on a bench or step and place the hands slightly wider than the shoulders on the floor.
Press up until the arms are straight and the body forms one line from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the floor under control, keeping the elbows angled back rather than flared.
Press back to straight arms, keeping the hips from sagging.
The higher the feet, the more the load shifts to the upper chest and shoulders.
coaching_cue: Feet elevated shifts the load toward the upper chest and shoulders.
clinical_rationale: Head-below-heart position with the shoulder near end range.
modification: Too hard? Use Push-Up. Too easy? Move to Pike Push-Up.

name: Dip Machine
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the lower chest, and select the assistance or load.
Sit tall, take the handles, and set the shoulders down away from the ears.
Press down until the arms are straight, keeping a slight forward lean.
Return under control until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
This is the assisted version of a dip — use it to build toward the real thing.
coaching_cue: The assisted version of a dip — use it to build toward the real thing.
clinical_rationale: Same shoulder position as a dip, with the load chosen rather than fixed.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with the knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand at the chest.
Set the shoulder blades down and the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press both dumbbells straight up until the arms lock out over the chest.
Lower until the backs of the upper arms touch the floor, then pause a beat.
Press again from that dead stop rather than bouncing off the ground.
coaching_cue: The floor caps the range, which is why this is the pressing option for a cranky shoulder.
clinical_rationale: As above. Deliberately untagged for the shoulder so that someone with a shoulder problem is left with a pressing option.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Flyes
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand directly above the chest, palms facing in.
Set a slight bend in the elbows and keep that angle fixed for the whole set.
Open the arms out in a wide arc until the chest lengthens and the elbows are level with the torso.
Stop there rather than chasing depth — the shoulder, not the chest, is what gives first.
Bring the dumbbells back together along the same arc, squeezing the chest at the top.
coaching_cue: A wide arc with soft elbows. If you can press it, it is too heavy for a fly.
clinical_rationale: Supine, and takes the shoulder to end-range horizontal abduction under load.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set a bench to about 30 degrees and lie back with the feet flat on the floor.
Pull the shoulder blades together and down and grip the bar a little wider than the shoulders.
Unrack the bar and hold it over the upper chest with straight arms.
Lower it to just below the collarbone with the elbows angled back.
Press back to straight arms — steeper than 30 degrees hands the set to the front shoulder.
coaching_cue: Bar touches high on the chest, just under the collarbone.
clinical_rationale: Inclined rather than flat, but still a reclined position under a loaded bar.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.
anatomy_source: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set a bench to about 30 degrees and sit back with a dumbbell resting on each thigh.
Lie back and bring the dumbbells to either side of the upper chest.
Set the shoulder blades down and the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press both dumbbells up until the arms are straight above the upper chest.
Lower slowly until the upper arms are level with the torso.
coaching_cue: Thirty degrees is enough — steeper and the front delt takes the set.
clinical_rationale: Reclined, and the incline shifts load onto the front of the shoulder.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Pec Deck
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the shoulders when seated.
Sit back against the pad and take a handle in each hand with the elbows level with the shoulders.
Bring the arms together in front of the chest in a smooth arc.
Squeeze for a beat with the hands close together.
Open the arms back to the start under control, stopping when the chest lengthens.
coaching_cue: Elbows level with the shoulders; drop them and it becomes a press.
clinical_rationale: Seated and fixed-path at end-range shoulder abduction.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Band Chest Press
instructions: Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height, or run it across your upper back.
Hold an end in each hand with the elbows bent and the hands beside the chest.
Press both hands forward until the arms are straight, bringing the hands slightly together.
Pause, then return under control until the hands are back beside the chest.
coaching_cue: Step further from the anchor to make it harder — that is your weight stack.
clinical_rationale: Upright and light. The mildest press in the library and the one a pregnant practitioner can keep.
modification: Too hard? Use step closer to the anchor. Too easy? Move to Dumbbell Bench Press.

name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with the eyes under the bar and the feet flat on the floor.
Pull the shoulder blades together and down into the bench and keep them there.
Grip the bar a little wider than the shoulders and unrack it over the chest.
Lower the bar to the mid-chest with the elbows about 45 degrees from the body.
Press back up until the arms are straight, keeping the shoulder blades set.
coaching_cue: Shoulder blades pinched and down into the bench before the bar leaves the rack.

progression.harder: Barbell Bench Press with a pause on the chest

clinical_rationale: Supine, and the heaviest horizontal press available. Lying flat is avoided after the first trimester.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh.
Lie back, using the thighs to help bring the dumbbells to either side of the chest.
Set the shoulder blades together and down, with the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press both dumbbells up over the mid-chest until the arms are straight.
Lower slowly until the upper arms are level with the torso, taking about twice as long as the press.
coaching_cue: Wrists stacked over the elbows; the dumbbells travel over the mid-chest, not the throat.
clinical_rationale: Supine. Dumbbells allow a deeper stretch at the bottom than a bar.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Incline Push-Up
instructions: Place the hands slightly wider than the shoulders on a bench, step or sturdy table.
Walk the feet back until the body is one straight line from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the surface with the elbows angled about 45 degrees from the ribs.
Press back to straight arms without letting the hips sag or pike.
The higher the surface, the easier it is — lower it as you get stronger.
coaching_cue: The higher the surface, the easier it is — lower it as you get stronger.
clinical_rationale: The most prenatal-friendly press: upright, self-limiting, no supine position.
modification: Too hard? Use Knee Push-Up. Too easy? Move to Push-Up.

name: Knee Push-Up
instructions: Kneel on a mat and place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders, fingers spread.
Walk your knees back until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Brace your trunk, then bend the elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Keep the elbows angled about 45 degrees from your body rather than flared wide.
Press the floor away until the arms are straight, without letting the hips sag or pike.
coaching_cue: Squeeze the glutes — it stops the low back sagging and makes the trunk do its job.
clinical_rationale: As the push-up, with less load through the wrist and shoulder.
modification: Too hard? Use Incline Push-Up against a wall. Too easy? Move to Incline Push-Up on a bench.

name: Machine Bench Press
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the mid-chest when you sit down.
Sit back with the whole spine against the pad and the feet flat on the floor.
Take the handles and set the shoulder blades down away from the ears.
Press forward until the arms are straight, without letting the shoulders round forward.
Return slowly until the hands are level with the chest.
coaching_cue: Set the seat so the handles sit at mid-chest height.
clinical_rationale: Supine and fixed-path; the path is what a restricted shoulder cannot adjust.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Push-Up
instructions: Lie face down and place the hands slightly wider than the shoulders, level with the mid-chest.
Tuck the toes under and press up until the arms are straight and the body is one line from head to heels.
Lower under control until the chest is a few centimetres off the floor, elbows angled about 45 degrees from the ribs.
Press the floor away to return to straight arms without letting the hips sag or pike.
Keep the neck long — look at a spot on the floor slightly ahead of the hands.
coaching_cue: One line from ear to ankle; the hips move with the chest, not before it.
clinical_rationale: Loaded wrist extension. Trunk stays off the floor, so it is workable in pregnancy for as long as the belly allows.
modification: Too hard? Use Incline Push-Up. Too easy? Move to Decline Push-Up.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel on a mat and hold the wheel handles under the shoulders, arms straight.
Brace the trunk and tuck the pelvis so the low back is flat, not arched.
Roll the wheel forward only as far as you can hold that flat back position.
Pull through the abdominals to draw the wheel back to the starting position.
If the low back arches at any point, shorten the range — that distance is your working range.
coaching_cue: Only roll as far as you can keep the low back flat. That distance is your range.
clinical_rationale: The longest anti-extension lever there is, with the shoulders holding the position.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Bird Dog
instructions: Start on hands and knees with the wrists under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Brace the trunk so the low back is flat and the hips are square to the floor.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with the torso.
Reach long rather than high, and do not let the hips rotate.
Return under control and repeat on the other side.
coaching_cue: Reach long rather than high, and keep the hips square to the floor.

progression.easier: extend only the arm, or only the leg
progression.harder: Bird Dog with a pause at full extension

clinical_rationale: Quadruped, low load, spine neutral. Safe for essentially everyone, including prenatally.
modification: Too hard? Use extend only the arm, or only the leg. Too easy? Move to Bird Dog with a pause at full extension.

name: Cable Crunch
instructions: Kneel facing a high pulley and hold a rope beside the head with both hands.
Set the hips back so there is tension on the cable before you move.
Curl the spine down, bringing the ribs toward the hips.
Keep the hips still — folding at the hips turns this into a different exercise.
Return slowly, letting the spine extend under the cable's pull.
coaching_cue: Curl the spine down rather than folding at the hips.
clinical_rationale: Weighted spinal flexion — the highest-load flexion movement in the library.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Crunches
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor.
Rest the hands lightly beside the head without pulling on the neck.
Curl the ribs toward the hips, lifting the shoulder blades a few centimetres off the floor.
Pause at the top and breathe out.
Lower slowly until the shoulder blades touch down.
coaching_cue: Curl the ribs toward the hips; do not yank on your own neck.
clinical_rationale: Repeated loaded spinal flexion. Abdominal separation makes this unsuitable prenatally.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on your back with the arms straight above the shoulders and the knees over the hips, bent to 90 degrees.
Press the low back firmly into the floor and hold it there for the whole set.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Stop the moment the low back begins to lift — that is your range.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side.
coaching_cue: Low back stays pressed to the floor the whole time. That is the entire exercise.

progression.easier: keep the knees bent and move one limb at a time

clinical_rationale: Supine. One of the better trunk drills for a sensitive back, since the range is set by the back staying flat.
modification: Too hard? Use keep the knees bent and move one limb at a time. Too easy? Move to Hollow Body Hold.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
instructions: Stand tall with one dumbbell in one hand and the other hand resting on the hip.
Keep the feet hip-width apart and the shoulders square to the front.
Bend sideways toward the weighted side, letting the dumbbell travel down the leg.
Return upright by pulling with the opposite side of the trunk.
Hold only one dumbbell — holding two cancels the movement out.
coaching_cue: One dumbbell only — holding two cancels the movement out.
clinical_rationale: Loaded lateral flexion of the lumbar spine.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Exercise Ball Crunch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and walk the feet forward until the low back is supported on it.
Set the feet flat and about hip-width apart for a stable base.
Cross the arms over the chest to keep the hands away from the neck.
Curl the ribs toward the hips, lifting the shoulders off the ball.
Lower slowly and let the spine extend over the ball — that extra range is why you use it.
coaching_cue: The ball lets the spine extend past flat, which is the point of using it.
clinical_rationale: As the crunch, through a longer range.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Exercise Ball Pull-In
instructions: Start in a push-up position with the shins resting on an exercise ball.
Set the hands under the shoulders and brace the trunk so the hips are level.
Draw the knees toward the chest, rolling the ball forward.
Keep the hips from piking up toward the ceiling.
Extend the legs slowly back to the plank position.
coaching_cue: Start in a plank with the shins on the ball and keep the hips from piking.
clinical_rationale: Plank on an unstable base; the shoulders support throughout.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Farmer's Walk
instructions: Set a pair of heavy dumbbells or kettlebells on the floor at your sides.
Hinge at the hips to pick them up, keeping the chest up and the spine long.
Stand tall with the shoulders back and the ribs down, arms hanging at your sides.
Walk in a straight line with controlled steps for the prescribed distance.
Set the weights down under control rather than dropping them.
coaching_cue: Walk tall and do not let the weights swing. It trains the trunk and the grip together.
clinical_rationale: Load hangs from the shoulder girdle through the neck; the spine itself stays neutral and braced.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Glute Bridge March
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor.
Press through the heels to lift the hips into a bridge and hold them there.
Without letting the hips drop or tilt, lift one knee toward the chest.
Return that foot to the floor and repeat on the other side, alternating throughout.
coaching_cue: The hips must not dip when the foot leaves the floor. That is the whole test.
clinical_rationale: Supine bridge held while the trunk resists tilt.
modification: Too hard? Use Glute Bridge. Too easy? Move to Single Leg Glute Bridge.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and the shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
Tilt the pelvis back and brace before the legs move.
Raise both legs together until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Avoid swinging — if the body starts rocking, lower the range.
Lower the legs slowly to a full hang.
coaching_cue: Tilt the pelvis before the legs move, or the hip flexors take all of it.
clinical_rationale: Hanging loads the shoulder throughout; the pelvis must tilt before the legs move.
modification: Too hard? Use Lying Leg Raise. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Hollow Body Hold
instructions: Lie on your back with the arms overhead and the legs straight.
Press the low back firmly into the floor and hold it there.
Lift the shoulders and legs a few inches, keeping the back flat.
Hold, breathing shallowly, and stop the moment the low back lifts away.
coaching_cue: If the low back comes off the floor, bend the knees — do not just endure it.

progression.harder: Hollow Body Hold with the arms overhead

clinical_rationale: Supine with a long lever; the low back lifts the moment the trunk gives.
modification: Too hard? Use Dead Bug. Too easy? Move to Hollow Body Hold with the arms overhead.

name: Leg Raise on Parallel Bars
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with the forearms on the pads and the back against the rest.
Let the legs hang straight and set the shoulders down away from the ears.
Tilt the pelvis back, then raise the legs until the thighs are parallel to the floor.
Lift with the abdominals rather than swinging the legs up.
Lower slowly to a full hang before the next repetition.
coaching_cue: Support your weight on the forearms and lift with the abs, not a swing.
clinical_rationale: Supported on the forearms, so less shoulder load than hanging.
modification: Too hard? Use Lying Leg Raise. Too easy? Move to Hanging Leg Raise.

name: Lying Leg Raise
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs straight and the hands tucked under the hips.
Press the low back flat into the floor and hold it there.
Raise both legs together until they are vertical.
Lower them slowly, stopping the moment the low back begins to lift away.
Bend the knees to shorten the lever if you cannot hold the back flat.
coaching_cue: Hands under the hips, low back flat. Shorten the range before you let it arch.

progression.easier: bend the knees to shorten the lever

clinical_rationale: Supine with a long lever; the low back arches as soon as the abdominals are outmatched.
modification: Too hard? Use bend the knees to shorten the lever. Too easy? Move to Leg Raise on Parallel Bars.

name: Pallof Press
instructions: Set a handle on a pulley at chest height and stand side-on, a stride away from it.
Hold the handle at the chest with both hands and set the feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace the trunk, then press the hands straight out in front of the chest.
Resist the cable's pull to rotate you — not rotating is the entire exercise.
Return the hands to the chest under control, then change sides.
coaching_cue: The point is to NOT rotate. Stand far enough out that resisting is hard.
clinical_rationale: Anti-rotation: the trunk resists movement rather than producing it. Safe prenatally and with most back restrictions.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Plank
instructions: Lie face down and set the forearms on the floor with the elbows directly under the shoulders.
Tuck the toes under and lift the hips until the body is one straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze the glutes and brace the trunk as if about to be punched in the stomach.
Hold, breathing normally through the nose, without letting the hips sag or ride up.
Lower the knees to the floor to finish rather than collapsing out of the position.
coaching_cue: Squeeze glutes and quads. A plank you can hold for three minutes is too easy.
clinical_rationale: The trunk resists extension against gravity — a demand that rises sharply as the abdomen loads.
modification: Too hard? Use Plank from the knees. Too easy? Move to Plank with one foot lifted.

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with the knees bent and lean the torso back to about 45 degrees.
Hold the hands together in front of the chest and keep the chest tall.
Rotate the ribs and shoulders to one side, following the hands with the eyes.
Return through the middle and rotate to the other side.
Rotate the ribs, not just the arms, and keep the heels down if the low back complains.
coaching_cue: Rotate the ribs, not just the arms, and keep the chest tall.

progression.easier: keep the heels on the floor

clinical_rationale: Loaded rotation of a flexed spine — the position discs tolerate least.
modification: Too hard? Use keep the heels on the floor. Too easy? Move to Russian Twist holding a weight.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on one side with the forearm on the floor and the elbow under the shoulder.
Stack the feet, or stagger them for a wider base.
Press the forearm down and lift the hips until the body is a straight line.
Hold, breathing normally, then lower under control and change sides.
coaching_cue: Stack the shoulders and hips; do not let the top one roll forward.

progression.easier: drop to the bottom knee for support
progression.harder: Side Plank with the top leg raised

clinical_rationale: The supporting shoulder carries the bodyweight.
modification: Too hard? Use drop to the bottom knee for support. Too easy? Move to Side Plank with the top leg raised.

name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
instructions: Set a handle on a high pulley and stand side-on with the feet shoulder-width apart.
Take the handle in both hands above the far shoulder with the arms extended.
Pull down and across the body toward the opposite hip, pivoting the back foot.
Rotate through the hips and mid-back rather than the low back.
Return along the same path under control, then complete the side before changing.
coaching_cue: Rotate through the hips and mid-back, not the low back.
clinical_rationale: Rotation under load, though driven from the hips rather than the lumbar spine.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Suitcase Carry
instructions: Stand a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell on the floor beside one foot.
Hinge at the hips to pick it up in one hand, keeping the chest up.
Stand tall with the shoulders level — resist the pull to one side.
Walk in a straight line for the prescribed distance, then swap hands.
coaching_cue: Staying square against a load on one side is the whole exercise.
clinical_rationale: One-sided load the trunk resists laterally.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Child's Pose
instructions: Kneel on a mat and bring the big toes together, letting the knees fall wide.
Sit the hips back toward the heels and walk the hands forward along the floor.
Rest the forehead down and let the arms stay long and relaxed.
Breathe into the back of the ribs and let the shoulders soften with each exhale.
Walk the hands back in and sit up slowly to come out.
coaching_cue: Let the breath widen the back of the ribs.
clinical_rationale: Deep knee flexion in the kneeling position; the spine is unloaded.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Cat-Cow
instructions: Start on hands and knees with the wrists under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Inhale and let the belly drop as you lift the chest and tailbone.
Exhale and round the spine, drawing the chin and tailbone toward each other.
Move slowly with the breath rather than forcing either end of the range.
coaching_cue: Let the breath set the pace — inhale to arch, exhale to round.
clinical_rationale: Unloaded spinal movement through a self-selected range. Suitable prenatally.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Inchworm
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward and place the hands on the floor, bending the knees as much as you need to.
Walk the hands forward until you reach a plank position with the body in one line.
Hold for a beat, then walk the hands back toward the feet.
Roll up to standing and repeat, letting the legs straighten a little more each time.
coaching_cue: Walk the hands out to a plank and back; keep the legs as straight as comfort allows.
clinical_rationale: Loaded forward fold into a plank; the wrists carry bodyweight at the far end.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Wrist Circles
instructions: Extend both arms in front of you at shoulder height and make loose fists.
Circle the hands slowly in one direction, moving only at the wrist.
Keep the forearms still so the movement stays in the joint you are preparing.
Reverse the direction after ten to fifteen seconds.
coaching_cue: Thirty seconds before anything that loads the wrist.
clinical_rationale: Unloaded joint preparation.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Band Pull-Through
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at ankle height and stand facing away from it.
Reach between the legs and take the band in both hands, then step forward to build tension.
Push the hips back, letting the hands travel between the thighs with a long spine.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, squeezing the glutes at the top.
Finish with the ribs down rather than leaning back.
coaching_cue: Hips drive back and then forward; the band should brush the inner thighs.
clinical_rationale: Hinge pattern with the load pulling backwards rather than down — the least spinal compression of any hinge.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band. Too easy? Move to Barbell Hip Thrust.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with the upper back against a bench and a padded barbell across the hips.
Set the feet flat, about shoulder-width apart, with the shins vertical at the top of the movement.
Tuck the chin and keep the ribs down, then drive through the heels to lift the hips.
Finish with the hips level with the knees and the glutes squeezed hard.
Lower under control without letting the low back take over from the glutes.
coaching_cue: Chin tucked, ribs down, and finish with the hips level with the knees.
clinical_rationale: Spine stays neutral and supported, so the disc restriction is dropped; the low back still resists extension at the top.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Barbell Lunge
instructions: Set a barbell across the upper back as you would for a squat and stand tall.
Take a controlled step forward, roughly two-thirds of a metre.
Lower until both knees are bent to about 90 degrees and the front shin is close to vertical.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
Balance is the limit here rather than strength — go lighter than you think you need.
coaching_cue: Balance is the limiting factor here, not strength. Go lighter than you think.
clinical_rationale: Loaded single-leg work with a bar on the back — balance fails before the muscles do.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Barbell Step Ups
instructions: Set a box at or just below knee height and place a barbell across the upper back.
Stand facing the box and place one whole foot on it.
Drive through that heel to stand up on the box, keeping the torso upright.
Step down under control with the other foot, resisting the drop.
Complete the reps on one side before changing, and keep the box below knee height.
coaching_cue: Box height at or below knee level; higher turns it into a balance test.
clinical_rationale: As above with an axial load and a balance demand on top.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Calf Raises - With Bands
instructions: Sit or stand with the balls of the feet on the floor and a resistance band over the thighs or under the feet.
Take up the slack so there is tension before you move.
Press through the balls of the feet to raise the heels as high as they will go.
Hold the top position for a full second.
Lower slowly until the heels are back down — calves answer to time under tension, not to bouncing.
coaching_cue: Bands are enough here — calves care more about reps than load.

progression.harder: Standing Calf Raise on a step for full range

clinical_rationale: Lightest ankle loading available.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Step Ups
instructions: Set a box at or just below knee height and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Place one whole foot on the box, heel included.
Drive through that heel to stand up, keeping the torso upright and the dumbbells hanging.
Step down under control with the trailing foot — that is the half everyone rushes.
Complete the reps on one side before changing.
coaching_cue: Step down under control — that is the half everyone rushes.
clinical_rationale: Loaded single-leg knee extension; box height decides how much.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Front Barbell Squat
instructions: Rack the bar across the front of the shoulders and raise the elbows until the upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Step back and set the feet shoulder-width apart with the toes slightly out.
Brace hard and keep the elbows high — the moment they drop, the bar follows.
Sit straight down with an upright torso, knees tracking over the middle toes.
Drive through the whole foot to stand, keeping the elbows up all the way.
coaching_cue: Elbows high throughout — the moment they drop, the bar follows.
clinical_rationale: As the back squat, plus a rack position the shoulder and wrist must hold.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Set the arms at your sides and tuck the pelvis so the low back flattens.
Drive through the heels to lift the hips until the body forms one line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes at the top with the ribs down, not with the low back arched.
Lower under control until the hips just touch the floor.
coaching_cue: Finish with the ribs down and the glutes squeezed, not with the low back arched.
clinical_rationale: Supine, which rules it out after the first trimester. Otherwise among the gentlest hip movements.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Glute Kickback
instructions: Start on hands and knees with the wrists under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Brace the trunk so the low back stays flat and the hips stay square.
Keeping one knee bent at 90 degrees, drive that heel toward the ceiling.
Stop when the thigh is level with the torso — going higher arches the low back.
Lower under control and complete the reps before changing sides.
coaching_cue: Square the hips and drive the heel to the ceiling; keep the range small.
clinical_rationale: Quadruped position; the low back arches if the range is chased.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Good Morning
instructions: Set a light barbell across the upper back and stand with the feet hip-width apart.
Soften the knees and brace the trunk hard.
Push the hips back and hinge the torso forward with the spine long.
Stop as soon as the hamstrings tighten or the back begins to round — the honest range here is short.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, and use far less weight than feels necessary.
coaching_cue: Go far lighter than feels necessary. This one has a very short honest range.
clinical_rationale: Bar on the back through a hinge — the longest lever against the spine of anything here.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with the feet slightly wider than the hips and a kettlebell on the floor an arm's length ahead.
Hinge at the hips with a long spine, tip the bell toward you and hike it back between the legs.
Snap the hips forward to stand tall, letting the bell float up to about chest height.
Keep the arms relaxed — they are rope, the hips throw the bell.
Let it swing back between the legs as the hips hinge again, and keep the spine long throughout.
coaching_cue: It is a hinge, not a squat, and the arms are rope — the hips throw the bell.
clinical_rationale: Ballistic hinge; the spine decelerates the bell at the bottom of every rep.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Leg Extensions
instructions: Sit in the machine with the back against the pad and the knee joint level with the machine's pivot.
Set the ankle pad just above the top of the feet.
Straighten both legs until the knees are extended, without snapping into the lockout.
Pause for a second at the top and squeeze the thighs.
Lower slowly under control — swinging up and dropping down is where knees complain.
coaching_cue: Pause at the top. Swinging up and dropping down is where knees complain.
clinical_rationale: Open-chain knee extension puts shear through the joint that closed-chain work does not.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Lying Leg Curls
instructions: Lie face down on the machine with the knee joints level with the pivot.
Set the ankle pad just above the heels and take the handles.
Curl the heels toward the glutes as far as the machine allows.
Keep the hips pressed into the pad — lifting them means the weight is too heavy.
Lower slowly until the legs are almost straight.
coaching_cue: Hips stay down on the pad; lifting them means the weight is too heavy.
clinical_rationale: Prone position rules it out prenatally; hamstring loading at the knee otherwise.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit at the machine with the balls of the feet on the platform and the pads across the lower thighs.
Release the safety and let the heels drop below the platform until the calves lengthen.
Press through the balls of the feet to raise the heels as high as they will go.
Hold the top for a second.
Lower slowly — the bent knee shifts the work to the soleus, the deeper calf muscle.
coaching_cue: Bent knee shifts the work to the soleus — the deeper calf muscle.
clinical_rationale: Bent knee moves the work to the soleus; ankle range is the same.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Sit in the machine with the back against the pad and the knee joints level with the pivot.
Set the thigh pad down firmly and place the ankles over the lower pad.
Curl the heels down and under as far as the machine allows.
Pause at full contraction rather than snapping back.
Return slowly until the legs are almost straight.
coaching_cue: Pause at full contraction rather than snapping back.
clinical_rationale: Seated and supported, so it keeps the hamstring work without the prone position.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and the feet flat on the floor.
Lift one foot and hold that knee toward the chest, or extend the leg straight.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot to raise the hips.
Keep the hips level — the side that drops is the one that needs the work.
Lower under control and complete the reps before changing sides.
coaching_cue: Keep the hips level — the side that drops is the one that needs the work.
clinical_rationale: Supine, and the single-leg version asks the low back to resist rotation.
modification: Too hard? Use Glute Bridge. Too easy? Move to Barbell Hip Thrust.

name: Split Squat
instructions: Take a long step forward into a split stance and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Set both feet planted — you are moving straight up and down, not stepping.
Lower until the back knee approaches the floor and the front thigh is roughly parallel.
Keep the torso upright and the front shin close to vertical.
Drive through the front heel to stand, and finish the side before changing.
coaching_cue: Feet stay planted; you are moving straight up and down, not stepping.
clinical_rationale: Both feet planted, so the balance demand is low and the knee path is stable.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Stand tall with the balls of the feet on the floor or the edge of a step.
Hold a support lightly for balance if you need it.
Press through the balls of the feet to raise the heels as high as they will go.
Hold the top for a full second.
Lower slowly through the full range — calves answer to time under tension, not to bouncing.
coaching_cue: Full range, slow down. Calves answer to time under tension, not to bouncing.

progression.harder: single-leg calf raise off a step

clinical_rationale: Full ankle range under bodyweight.
modification: Too hard? Use both feet on flat ground. Too easy? Move to single-leg calf raise off a step.

name: Wall Sit
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall and walk the feet out about two foot-lengths.
Slide down the wall until the knees are bent to roughly ninety degrees.
Keep the shins vertical and the whole back in contact with the wall.
Hold, breathing normally, then walk the feet back in to stand up.
coaching_cue: If the knees pass the toes, walk the feet further out.

progression.easier: sit higher, with less knee bend
progression.harder: Wall Sit holding a weight on the lap

clinical_rationale: Sustained isometric knee flexion; the position is fixed and the load is bodyweight.
modification: Too hard? Use sit higher, with less knee bend. Too easy? Move to Wall Sit holding a weight on the lap.

name: Banded Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet hip-width apart.
Hold an end in each hand with the arms straight and the shoulders back.
Push the hips back and let the hands travel down the front of the legs, knees soft.
Stop when you feel the hamstrings lengthen, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.
coaching_cue: Hips back, not knees down. The band should stay against your legs.
clinical_rationale: Lightest hinge in the library; tension is lowest at the bottom where the spine is most flexed.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band. Too easy? Move to Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift.

name: Banded Squat
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet shoulder-width apart.
Bring the top of the band over the shoulders and hold it in place at chest height.
