Sit back and down into a squat, keeping the chest up and the knees tracking over the toes.
Drive through the heels to stand, resisting the band's pull all the way up.
coaching_cue: The band gets harder as you stand, which suits the squat well.
clinical_rationale: Band tension is highest standing and lowest at depth, which is the opposite of where the knee is loaded.
modification: Too hard? Use Bodyweight Squat. Too easy? Move to Goblet Squat.

name: Barbell Deadlift
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of the feet, shins nearly touching it.
Push the hips back and take an overhand grip just outside the knees.
Set the chest up, flatten the back and take the slack out of the bar before pulling.
Drive through the floor with the legs, keeping the bar against the legs the whole way up.
Finish standing tall with the hips locked, then push the hips back to lower it along the same path.
coaching_cue: The bar stays against the legs the whole way. If it swings out, reset.
clinical_rationale: The heaviest axial pull available, with a brace held against a maximal effort.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell at arm's length against the thighs, hands just outside the knees.
Set the knees softly bent and hold that bend throughout — this is a hinge, not a squat.
Push the hips back and let the bar travel down the front of the legs, keeping the spine long.
Stop when the hamstrings run out of length, usually around mid-shin.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, keeping the bar against the legs the whole way.
coaching_cue: Soft knees, long spine, hips travel back — this is a hamstring movement, not a squat.
clinical_rationale: Sustained loaded hinge; the hamstrings run out before the spine does, which is where it goes wrong.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Barbell Squat
instructions: Set the bar across the upper back, not the neck, and grip it firmly with the elbows down.
Step back and set the feet shoulder-width apart with the toes turned slightly out.
Brace the trunk as if about to be punched in the stomach.
Sit down and back between the hips, keeping the chest up and the knees tracking over the middle toes.
Descend to at least parallel if your hips allow it, then drive the floor away to stand.
coaching_cue: Brace as if about to be punched, then sit between the hips.
clinical_rationale: Axial load through the spine with a hard brace; the knee is at end-range flexion under that load.
modification: Too hard? Use Goblet Squat. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart and the toes turned slightly out.
Reach the arms forward for balance and set the chest up.
Sit down and back between the hips as though reaching for a low chair.
Keep the heels down and the knees tracking over the middle toes.
Descend as far as you can hold the position, then drive through the heels to stand tall.
coaching_cue: Sit back and down between the hips; knees track over the middle toes.
clinical_rationale: No external load; depth is self-selected.
modification: Too hard? Use Box Squat to a chair. Too easy? Move to Bulgarian Split Squat.

name: Box Squat to a Chair
instructions: Stand in front of a chair or bench with the feet about shoulder-width apart.
Reach the hips back and lower under control until you are seated.
Keep the chest up and the weight through the mid-foot rather than the toes.
Stand back up by driving through the heels, without rocking forward for momentum.
coaching_cue: Touch and go, do not flop. The chair sets the depth so you can build confidence in it.
clinical_rationale: The chair sets the depth, so the knee never passes into an unmanaged range.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand about two-thirds of a metre in front of a bench and place the top of one foot on it behind you.
Keep the torso upright and the front foot far enough forward that the knee stays over the ankle.
Lower until the back knee approaches the floor and the front thigh is roughly parallel.
Drive through the front heel to stand, completing all reps before changing sides.
coaching_cue: Almost all the work belongs to the front leg — the back foot is for balance only.
clinical_rationale: Deep single-leg flexion with the rear foot elevated; a demanding position for the front knee.
modification: Too hard? Use Reverse Lunge. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Dumbbell Lunges
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell hanging at each side and the feet hip-width apart.
Take a controlled step forward, about two-thirds of a metre, and lower the back knee toward the floor.
Stop when both knees are bent to roughly ninety degrees and the front shin is close to vertical.
Drive through the front heel to push back to the starting position.
Alternate legs, keeping the torso upright and the dumbbells hanging still.
coaching_cue: Weights hang at the sides; let the legs do the work, not the shoulders.
clinical_rationale: Single-leg knee flexion under load; the dumbbells can be dropped, which the bar cannot.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of the thighs.
Set the knees softly bent and keep that bend for the whole set.
Push the hips back and let the dumbbells travel down the front of the legs.
Keep the spine long and the dumbbells in contact with the legs throughout.
Stop when the hamstrings run out of length, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.
coaching_cue: Push the hips back and keep the weights against the thighs. Stop when the hamstrings run out.
clinical_rationale: Same hinge, lighter load, dumbbells tracking closer to the body.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against the chest with both hands under the top of it.
Set the feet shoulder-width apart with the toes turned slightly out.
Keep the elbows tucked in and the chest tall — the weight at the chest is what keeps you upright.
Sit down between the hips, letting the elbows travel inside the knees.
Drive through the whole foot to stand, keeping the weight against the chest throughout.
coaching_cue: Holding the weight at the chest keeps you upright — it is the best squat to learn on.
clinical_rationale: The chest-held weight keeps the torso upright and the load light. The squat that survives most restrictions.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Hack Squat
instructions: Set yourself in the machine with the back flat against the pad and the shoulders under the supports.
Place the feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safeties and lower by bending the knees, keeping the whole back on the pad.
Descend until the thighs are roughly parallel, or until the low back starts to lift.
Drive through the whole foot to press back up without locking the knees hard at the top.
coaching_cue: Back flat on the pad throughout; the machine holds the position for you.
clinical_rationale: Fixed path holds the knee in one line whether or not that is the practitioner's line.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the machine with the whole back and hips against the pad.
Place the feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safeties and lower the platform by bending the knees toward the chest.
Stop the moment the low back begins to lift off the pad — that is your depth limit.
Press back up through the whole foot without locking the knees out hard.
coaching_cue: Do not let the low back round off the pad at the bottom — that is the depth limit.
clinical_rationale: Deep knee flexion under heavy load; the low back rounds off the pad at depth.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the hands on the hips.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees are bent to about ninety degrees.
Keep the front shin close to vertical and the torso upright.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing, then alternate sides.
coaching_cue: Stepping back rather than forward is much kinder to the knee.
clinical_rationale: Stepping back rather than forward keeps the front shin vertical and is markedly kinder to the knee.
modification: Too hard? Use Split Squat holding a support. Too easy? Move to Bulgarian Split Squat.

name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Set the feet well wider than the shoulders with the toes turned out, bar over the mid-foot.
Push the hips down and back and take an overhand grip inside the knees.
Set the chest up, flatten the back and pull the slack out of the bar.
Drive the floor apart with the feet and open the hips as the bar rises.
Finish standing tall, then push the hips back to lower the bar along the same path.
coaching_cue: Wide stance, hands inside the knees, and open the hips as you pull.
clinical_rationale: As the conventional pull, with the wide stance loading the hip in abduction.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: 90/90 Hamstring
instructions: Lie on your back beside a doorway or wall with one leg flat on the floor.
Raise the other leg and rest the heel against the wall with the hip and knee both bent to 90 degrees.
Slowly straighten that knee until you feel the hamstring lengthen.
Hold there and breathe — ease off the moment it turns sharp.
Bend the knee to release, then change sides.
coaching_cue: Hold thirty seconds and breathe. A stretch is not a set.
clinical_rationale: Passive stretch against a wall, range self-selected.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Adductor
instructions: Sit on the floor and bring the soles of the feet together, letting the knees fall out to the sides.
Hold the ankles and sit tall through the spine.
Ease the knees toward the floor using the weight of the legs rather than forcing them.
Hold and breathe, keeping the back long rather than rounding over.
Bring the knees back together with the hands to come out of it.
coaching_cue: Ease into it. Bouncing at the end range achieves nothing.
clinical_rationale: End-range hip abduction; the load is the weight of the legs.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with the legs straight and the forehead resting on one forearm.
Bend one knee and reach back with the free hand to hold the ankle or foot.
Draw the heel gently toward the glute until the front of the thigh lengthens.
Keep the hips square and pressed to the floor rather than rolling to one side.
Hold and breathe, then release slowly and change sides.
coaching_cue: Keep the knees together and the hips square.
clinical_rationale: End-range knee flexion, performed lying face down.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Seated Glute
instructions: Sit tall on a chair or bench with both feet flat on the floor.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee so the shin is roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep the crossed leg's knee relaxed out to the side.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine until the glute lengthens.
Hold and breathe, then sit up slowly and change sides.
coaching_cue: Sit tall and hinge forward from the hips, not the low back.
clinical_rationale: Passive hip external rotation with a forward hinge.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Standing Hip Circles
instructions: Stand tall and hold a support with one hand for balance.
Lift one knee to about hip height in front of you.
Draw slow circles with that knee, opening the hip out to the side and back.
Keep the standing leg soft and the torso upright rather than leaning away.
Reverse the direction, then change sides.
coaching_cue: Hold a support if you need it and keep the circles slow.
clinical_rationale: Unloaded joint preparation through the hip's own range.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Arnold Dumbbell Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest height, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating the palms outward, so they face forward at the top.
Finish with the arms straight overhead and the ribs down.
Reverse the path exactly, rotating the palms back toward you as you lower.
Use less weight than a straight press — the rotation is what costs you.
coaching_cue: Rotate as you press, and go lighter than a straight press — the rotation costs you.
clinical_rationale: Adds internal-to-external rotation under load, through the arc the cuff is most exposed in.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Band Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet hip-width apart.
Hold an end in each hand at your sides with the palms facing in.
Lead with the elbows and raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Stop level with the shoulders rather than going higher.
Lower slowly against the band — with bands the lowering half is the useful half.
coaching_cue: Slow on the way down — bands make the lowering half the useful half.
clinical_rationale: Lightest abduction available; band tension is least where the arc is most sensitive.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band. Too easy? Move to Side Lateral Raise.

name: Bent Over Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Sit on the end of a bench and hinge forward until the chest rests near the thighs.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand hanging beneath the shoulders, palms facing each other.
Think of pulling the dumbbells apart rather than lifting them up.
Raise the arms out to the sides until level with the shoulders, elbows softly bent.
Lower slowly — this is a small muscle, so the weight should be small too.
coaching_cue: Think of pulling the dumbbells apart rather than lifting them up.
clinical_rationale: Posterior shoulder work, which is generally protective. Hinged position rules it out prenatally.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.
anatomy_source: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set a pulley at the lowest position and stand side-on with the handle in the far hand.
Let the arm hang across the front of the body with light tension on the cable.
Lead with the elbow and raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Stop level with the shoulder and pause briefly.
Lower slowly, keeping tension at the bottom, then change sides.
coaching_cue: Same movement as the dumbbell version, with tension at the bottom too.
clinical_rationale: As the dumbbell version, with tension held at the bottom.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Set two pulleys at shoulder height and stand between them.
Take the left handle in the right hand and the right handle in the left, arms crossed in front.
Keep the elbows softly bent and fixed at that angle.
Pull the arms out and back until they are level with the shoulders and wide open.
Return slowly across the body — the cable keeps tension where dumbbells lose it.
coaching_cue: Constant tension is the advantage the cable has over dumbbells here.
clinical_rationale: Standing and upright, so it keeps the posterior work without the hinge.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Face Pull
instructions: Set a rope attachment on a cable pulley at roughly face height and take an end in each hand.
Step back until the arms are extended and there is tension on the cable, thumbs pointing back.
Pull the rope toward your forehead, driving the elbows high and wide and separating the hands.
Pause briefly with the hands beside the ears and the shoulder blades squeezed together.
Return to full arm extension under control, letting the shoulder blades travel forward.
coaching_cue: Rope to the forehead, elbows high. This is the movement that keeps pressing pain-free.
clinical_rationale: External rotation with abduction — the movement most often prescribed FOR a shoulder, not against it.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Front Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of the thighs.
Keep the elbows softly bent and the trunk braced.
Raise one arm forward to shoulder height, palm facing down.
Stop level with the shoulder rather than swinging higher.
Lower slowly and alternate arms, resisting the urge to rock the hips.
coaching_cue: Stop at shoulder height and resist the swing on the way down.
clinical_rationale: Flexion to shoulder height with a long lever.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Pike Push-Up - Feet Elevated
instructions: Set the feet on a box or a chair and walk the hands back until the hips are stacked high.
Place the hands slightly wider than the shoulders with the fingers spread.
Lower the crown of the head toward the floor between the hands.
Press back to straight arms, keeping the hips high throughout.
coaching_cue: The closest a home setup gets to an overhead press with real load.
clinical_rationale: Near-vertical loading with the head well below the heart.
modification: Too hard? Use Pike Push-Up. Too easy? Move to Wall Handstand Hold.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap
instructions: Start in a push-up position with the hands under the shoulders and the feet wide.
Brace the trunk so the hips are level and square to the floor.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder without letting the hips rotate.
Return the hand to the floor and repeat on the other side, alternating throughout.
coaching_cue: Widen the feet if the hips twist. Not rotating is the work.

progression.easier: widen the feet, or drop to the knees
progression.harder: Plank Shoulder Tap with the feet together

clinical_rationale: Loaded wrist extension in a plank; the plank position is unavailable as the abdomen loads.
modification: Too hard? Use widen the feet, or drop to the knees. Too easy? Move to Plank Shoulder Tap with the feet together.

name: Prone T-Raise
instructions: Lie face down with the arms out to the sides at shoulder height, forming a T.
Turn the thumbs up toward the ceiling.
Lift both arms by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly without resting the hands down.
coaching_cue: Rear delts and mid-back. Small range, done properly, beats a big sloppy one.
clinical_rationale: Light posterior shoulder work, performed face down.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Prone Y-Raise
instructions: Lie face down on a mat or an incline bench with the arms extended overhead in a Y shape.
Turn the thumbs up toward the ceiling.
Lift both arms a few inches by squeezing the muscles between the shoulder blades.
Hold for a second at the top, then lower slowly without letting the hands touch down.
coaching_cue: Height is not the goal. Two inches done well beats six done with the low back.
clinical_rationale: As the T-raise, with more shoulder flexion.
modification: Too hard? Use Prone T-Raise. Too easy? Move to Reverse Flyes.

name: Reverse Flyes
instructions: Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Let the arms hang beneath the shoulders with the thumbs pointing down.
Keep the elbows softly bent and fixed at that angle.
Raise the arms out to the sides until level with the shoulders.
Lower slowly, keeping the torso still rather than rocking up with each rep.
coaching_cue: Thumbs down, elbows soft, and stop when the arms reach shoulder line.
clinical_rationale: As the rear delt raise.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Side Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Keep the elbows softly bent and the trunk braced.
Lead with the elbows and raise both arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Stop level with the shoulders — higher hands the work to the traps.
Lower slowly. This is a small muscle, so keep the weight light.
coaching_cue: Lead with the elbows to shoulder height. Light weight — this is a small muscle.
clinical_rationale: Abduction to shoulder height. Light, but directly through the painful arc.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Upright Row
instructions: Stand holding a barbell at arm's length with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Keep the bar close to the body and lead with the elbows as you pull it upward.
Stop when the upper arms reach shoulder height — no higher.
Pause briefly, then lower the bar under control to full arm extension.
coaching_cue: Stop at shoulder height. Pulling to the chin is where shoulders get pinched.
clinical_rationale: Internal rotation with the arm abducted — the classic impingement position.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Wall Handstand Hold
instructions: Place the hands about a foot from a wall, shoulder-width apart.
Walk the feet up the wall until the body is close to vertical and the arms are straight.
Push the floor away, keep the ribs down and hold, breathing steadily.
Walk back down under control before the shoulders give out.
coaching_cue: Come down before you have to. This one does not warn you twice.
clinical_rationale: Full inversion under bodyweight; blood pressure and wrist load are both at their limit.
modification: Too hard? Use Pike Push-Up - Feet Elevated. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Band Overhead Press
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet hip-width apart.
Hold an end in each hand at shoulder height with the palms facing forward.
Brace the trunk and press both hands overhead until the arms are straight.
Lower back to shoulder height under control, resisting the band on the way down.
coaching_cue: Ribs down. If the low back arches to finish the press, the band is too strong.
clinical_rationale: Overhead, but band tension is lowest at the bottom and the load is small.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band. Too easy? Move to Dumbbell Shoulder Press.

name: Barbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Set a barbell at shoulder height and take an overhand grip just outside the shoulders.
Unrack it to the front of the shoulders and stand tall with the feet hip-width apart.
Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down so the press does not become a standing backbend.
Press the bar overhead, moving the head back slightly to let it pass, then through as it locks out.
Lower under control to the front of the shoulders before the next repetition.
coaching_cue: Head moves back to let the bar pass, then through as it locks out overhead.
clinical_rationale: Overhead pressing with a bar; the bracing required raises intrathoracic pressure.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Turn the palms to face forward with the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Set the ribs down and brace the trunk.
Press both dumbbells overhead until the arms are straight.
Lower under control to shoulder height without letting the low back arch.
coaching_cue: Ribs down, glutes tight — the press should not turn into a standing backbend.
clinical_rationale: Overhead, but seated and independently loaded so the arms find their own path.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Hands-Elevated Pike Push-Up
instructions: Place the hands on a bench, chair or low table and walk the feet back.
Push the hips up and back until the torso and arms form a straight line.
Bend the elbows to lower the head toward the raised surface between the hands.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping the hips high the whole time.
coaching_cue: Hands high makes it easier. This is where an overhead press starts with no equipment.
clinical_rationale: Less overhead load and less inversion than the floor version.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the shoulders when seated.
Sit back with the whole spine against the pad and the feet flat.
Take the handles with the palms facing forward and the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press overhead until the arms are straight, without shrugging the shoulders up.
Lower under control until the hands are back level with the shoulders.
coaching_cue: The supported option — a good place to press from if balance is the limit.
clinical_rationale: Supported and fixed-path; suitable when balance rather than the shoulder is the limit.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Pike Push-Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position and walk the feet in until the hips are high and the body forms an inverted V.
Set the hands slightly wider than the shoulders with the fingers spread.
Bend the elbows to lower the crown of the head toward the floor between the hands.
Keep the hips high throughout — letting them drop turns this back into a push-up.
Press back to the starting position until the arms are straight.
coaching_cue: Feet closer to the hands means more of your weight overhead, which is the progression.

progression.harder: Pike Push-Up with the feet on a box

clinical_rationale: Bodyweight overhead press with the head below the heart.
modification: Too hard? Use Incline Push-Up. Too easy? Move to Pike Push-Up with the feet on a box.

name: Push Press
instructions: Take a barbell from a rack at shoulder height with the hands just outside the shoulders.
Stand tall with the elbows slightly in front of the bar and the trunk braced.
Dip a few inches by bending the knees, keeping the torso upright.
Drive up hard through the legs and let that momentum start the bar overhead.
Finish the movement with the arms until the bar is locked out above the mid-foot.
Lower the bar back to the shoulders under control and reset before the next rep.
coaching_cue: A short dip and drive from the legs, then the arms finish it overhead.
clinical_rationale: Explosive overhead drive with an axial load and a hard brace.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Arm Circles
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
Make small circles forward, about the size of a dinner plate, keeping the arms long.
Gradually widen the circles over ten to fifteen seconds.
Reverse the direction and repeat, keeping the shoulders down away from the ears.
coaching_cue: Small circles first, then larger — this is joint preparation, not a set.
clinical_rationale: Unloaded joint preparation.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Band Pull Apart
instructions: Hold a resistance band with both hands, arms extended straight in front at chest height.
Set the hands about shoulder-width apart so there is light tension on the band.
Keeping the arms long, pull the hands apart until the band touches the chest.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together and hold for a beat.
Return slowly to the start — this is the best two minutes you can spend before pressing.
coaching_cue: Arms long, squeeze the shoulder blades. Best thing you can do before pressing.
clinical_rationale: Scapular retraction against light resistance. Safe for essentially everyone.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: External Rotation
instructions: Stand or sit holding a light dumbbell in one hand with the elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Pin that elbow against your side and keep it there for the whole set.
Rotate the forearm outward, away from the body, as far as is comfortable.
Return slowly to the front — only the forearm moves.
Two to five kilos is the whole useful range here; this is a cuff drill, not a lift.
coaching_cue: Elbow pinned to the ribs. Two to five kilos is the whole range here — this is a cuff drill, not a lift.
clinical_rationale: Rotator-cuff rehab loading. Deliberately untagged: withholding it from a shoulder problem removes the treatment.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Wall Slide
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and the feet a few inches out from it.
Place the forearms on the wall with the elbows at shoulder height.
Slide the arms up the wall as far as you can without the low back arching away.
Slide back down slowly, keeping the forearms in contact throughout.
coaching_cue: Best two minutes you can spend before pressing anything overhead.
clinical_rationale: Scapular rehab drill against a wall. The derived rule withheld it from shoulder problems, which is backwards.
modification: Ease into the range; never stretch into pain.

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Anchor a band overhead and hold an end in each hand.
Stand tall with the elbows tucked at your sides and bent to about ninety degrees.
Push the hands down until the arms are straight, keeping the elbows still.
Let the band draw the hands back up under control.
coaching_cue: Only the forearms move. If the elbows travel, drop the tension.
clinical_rationale: Lightest elbow extension available.
modification: Too hard? Use a lighter band. Too easy? Move to Triceps Pushdown.

name: Bench Dips
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench and place the hands beside the hips, fingers forward.
Slide the hips forward off the bench with the legs extended or the knees bent.
Keep the hips close to the bench and lower by bending the elbows straight back.
Stop when the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Press back to straight arms — drifting away from the bench is what strains the shoulder.
coaching_cue: Keep the hips close to the bench — drifting away is what strains the shoulder.

progression.easier: bend the knees and keep the feet close

clinical_rationale: Internally rotated shoulder behind the torso — a poor position under load.
modification: Too hard? Use bend the knees and keep the feet close. Too easy? Move to Chest Dip.

name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
instructions: Set your hands shoulder-width apart on a bench, low bar or sturdy table edge.
Walk the feet back so the body is straight and leaning into the surface.
Keeping the upper arms still and pointing forward, bend only the elbows to lower the forehead toward your hands.
Press back to straight arms by extending the elbows, without letting the hips sag.
coaching_cue: Only the elbows move. Walk the feet back to make it harder, in toward the surface to make it easier.

progression.easier: walk the feet in toward the surface

clinical_rationale: Self-limiting, but the elbow is the only joint working.
modification: Too hard? Use walk the feet in toward the surface. Too easy? Move to Diamond Push-Up.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a push-up position with the hands directly under the shoulders.
Tuck the toes under and hold the body in one straight line from head to heels.
Lower the chest with the elbows tracking back along the ribs, not flaring out.
Stop just short of the floor, then press back to straight arms.
Keeping the elbows close is what moves the work to the triceps.
coaching_cue: Elbows stay close to the ribs — that is what moves the work to the triceps.
clinical_rationale: Loaded wrist extension with the elbows tracking close.
modification: Too hard? Use Incline Close-Grip Push-Up. Too easy? Move to Diamond Push-Up.

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position and bring the hands together so index fingers and thumbs form a diamond.
Set the hands under the chest rather than under the face.
Lower the chest toward the hands, keeping the elbows tracking back rather than flaring.
Press back up to straight arms without letting the hips sag.
coaching_cue: Hard on the wrists — drop to the knees before you compromise the position.
clinical_rationale: The narrowest hand position puts the wrist at its end range.
modification: Too hard? Use Close-Grip Push-Up. Too easy? Add load or slow the tempo.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension - Two Hands
instructions: Sit or stand tall and hold one dumbbell vertically in both hands, palms under the top plate.
Press it overhead until the arms are straight, elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Keeping the upper arms still, lower the dumbbell behind the head.
Go until you feel the triceps lengthen, without letting the elbows flare wide.
Press back to straight arms — one dumbbell in both hands is steadier than two.
coaching_cue: One dumbbell in both hands is steadier than two, especially when heavy.
clinical_rationale: As above; two hands make it steadier, not lighter on the shoulder.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar over the chest with a close overhand grip.
Angle the upper arms slightly back toward the head rather than straight up.
Keeping the upper arms still, bend the elbows to lower the bar toward the forehead.
Stop at the forehead or just behind it.
Extend the elbows to press back up, keeping the upper arms in the same place throughout.
coaching_cue: Upper arms angled slightly back keeps tension on through the top.
clinical_rationale: As above, with the angled bar easing the wrist only.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Lying Triceps Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell over the chest with a close overhand grip.
Angle the upper arms slightly back toward the head and keep them there.
Bend the elbows to lower the bar to the forehead or just behind it.
Keep the upper arms still — only the forearms move.
Extend the elbows to press the bar back to the starting position.
coaching_cue: Lower to the forehead or just behind it, and keep the upper arms still.
clinical_rationale: Supine, and loads the elbow at end-range flexion.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: One-Arm Cable Pushdown
instructions: Set a single handle on a high pulley and stand facing the machine.
Take the handle in one hand and tuck that elbow against your side.
Push the hand down until the arm is straight, keeping the elbow still.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom for a beat.
Return under control and complete the set before changing sides.
coaching_cue: One side at a time finds the weaker arm quickly.
clinical_rationale: As the pushdown, one side at a time.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in one hand, pressed overhead with a straight arm.
Point the elbow at the ceiling and brace the trunk so the ribs stay down.
Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind the head.
Keep the upper arm still and vertical throughout.
Extend the elbow to press back overhead, then change sides.
coaching_cue: Elbows point at the ceiling and stay there.
clinical_rationale: Overhead position stretches the long head and loads the shoulder to hold it there.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
instructions: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, torso parallel to the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in the free hand and raise that upper arm until it is level with the torso.
Keep the upper arm fixed there for the whole set.
Extend the elbow to straighten the arm behind you and squeeze the triceps.
Return to 90 degrees under control — only the forearm moves.
coaching_cue: Upper arm parallel to the floor and still; only the forearm moves.
clinical_rationale: Short lever, light load, elbow working in mid-range.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Triceps Overhead Extension with Rope
instructions: Set a rope on a low pulley and face away from the machine, rope held overhead.
Step forward into a split stance with the elbows pointing ahead and bent behind the head.
Keeping the upper arms still, extend the elbows until the arms are straight overhead.
Pull the ends of the rope apart at the top.
Return slowly behind the head — the overhead position stretches the part pushdowns miss.
coaching_cue: Overhead position stretches the long head — the part pushdowns miss.
clinical_rationale: Overhead under constant cable tension.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and stand facing the machine, feet hip-width apart.
Take an overhand grip and tuck the elbows firmly against your sides.
Push the bar down until the arms are straight, keeping the elbows still.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom for a beat.
Return until the forearms are just above parallel, without letting the elbows travel forward.
coaching_cue: Elbows locked to the ribs; only the forearms move.
clinical_rationale: Standing and self-limiting, but the elbow is the working joint.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar just inside shoulder width.
Set the shoulder blades together and down and unrack the bar over the chest.
Lower it to the lower chest, keeping the elbows tucked close to the ribs.
Press back to straight arms, driving through the triceps.
Any narrower than shoulder width and the wrists pay for it.
coaching_cue: Hands just inside shoulder width. Any closer and the wrists pay for it.
clinical_rationale: Supine press; the narrow grip concentrates load at the elbow.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.

name: Incline Close-Grip Push-Up
instructions: Place the hands close together on a bench, step or sturdy table.
Walk the feet back until the body is one straight line from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the hands with the elbows tracking back along the ribs.
Press back to straight arms without letting the hips sag.
The higher the surface, the easier it is — this is the triceps push-up a beginner can do.
coaching_cue: Hands close and elevated — the triceps push-up a beginner can actually do.
clinical_rationale: Elevated hands reduce both the load and the wrist angle.
modification: Slow the tempo or pause a beat to make it harder; shorten the range or reduce the load if form breaks down.
